explanation: `nats zero succ` is the library's own definition: the least fixed point (`lfpSet`) of its `genOp zero succ`, i.e. the intersection of all sets containing zero and closed under succ. The theorem says this set is closed under `succ`. The proof just unfolds that definition. I did not search Mathlib. I judged that no Mathlib declaration states closure of this custom set. I did not check whether Mathlib has a generic lemma about the intersection of all sets closed under a map, but the theorem's content lies in the library's own definition.
